# Security Scanning

DevDesk orchestrates three external security tools — Trivy, Gitleaks, and
plumber — against local repositories and container images, caches their
results, and surfaces everything through a unified security inventory view.
This page explains the model behind that orchestration: how tools are
located, how results from different tools are merged into one taxonomy, and
how the two-tier cache stays consistent across scans launched from different
screens.

## Locating the tools

Each tool's location is a declared setting, not an autodetected fact.
`scan.tools.<tool>.source` — for `trivy`, `gitleaks`, `plumber`,
`kubeconform`, `helm` and `kustomize` alike — takes one of:

| Value | Resolution |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | the binary if present, else the Docker image |
| `binary` | the configured path, or the name on `PATH` — **fails outright** if not found, rather than silently falling back to Docker |
| `image` | always the configured Docker image, even if a binary is installed |

`scan.Detect` resolves every tool into a `Report`, and `Report.Spec(tool)`
produces a `ToolSpec` (source + binary path + image) that command builders consume directly, rather than threading
a raw `(source, image)` pair through several layers and hoping a configured
path gets read somewhere along the way.

The choice to fail loudly in `binary` mode is deliberate: silently falling
back to Docker is exactly what would make a misconfigured path invisible —
the scan keeps "working," just with a different tool than the one requested.

- **Remediation tab** — newer tags for each Dockerfile base image. `S` scans the candidates, `space` chooses one per stage, `enter` shows the diff, `ctrl+o` writes it.
- **Misconfigurations tab** — `ctrl+o` on a finding the built-in catalog covers (a missing `USER`, `ADD` instead of `COPY`, a missing `--no-cache`…) writes the fix, then re-scans to check that the rule is gone.

For anything else, an AI client connected over [MCP](connect-an-ai-client.md) can read the finding, edit the file and re-scan. See [Remediation](../explanation/scanning.md#remediation).

## Why results might be stale

The cache is keyed by repository/image, not by commit — a scan result stays valid until you rescan, even if the underlying code has changed since. If you want to be sure you're looking at current findings, press `S` before reading `:sec`.

Deleted repositories and images drop out of the Security view and the dashboard's counts automatically; a cached result for something that no longer exists is never shown as current.

## Configure which checks run

```yaml
scan:
  categories:
    vuln:      { enabled: true,  tools: [trivy] }            # CVEs
    secret:    { enabled: true,  tools: [trivy, gitleaks] }  # secrets
    misconfig: { enabled: true,  tools: [trivy] }            # IaC misconfiguration
    license:   { enabled: false, tools: [trivy] }            # license issues
  tools:
    trivy:    { ignore_unfixed: false }  # drop CVEs with no available fix
    gitleaks: { history: false }         # scan full git history, not just the working tree
```

These same settings are editable in the configuration view (`:config`, the
`scan` tab) — no need to hand-edit YAML for a one-off change. A category runs
the tools ticked in it; a ticked tool that cannot run is reported by the scan
that needed it. See the [configuration reference](../reference/configuration.md)
for the full `scan:` schema, including Trivy server mode
(`tools.trivy.server`).

  to it. DevDesk's own registry calls (`internal/oci`) go through the entry point.

  it with libcurl's rules, not Go's. libcurl ignores an upper case `HTTP_PROXY`
  for `http://` URLs (only `http_proxy` counts), reads `all_proxy`, and its

  the only place that builds `<engine> run --rm`. Its `cmd()` writes

  `gitleaks.go`, `cosign.go`, `plumber.go`, `kubeconform.go`,

  returns a `Forward`, a snapshot of `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`
  taken once. For each of the three, the first non-empty value of the upper then
  lower case name is given to both casings. `cmd()` adds `-e NAME` (no value) for
  each name, in the order of `ForwardedVariables`, and sets the values on the
  child process through `Forward.Environ(os.Environ())` (the six names are
  removed from the base first). The engine copies the client's value, so a
  credential in a proxy URL is in no argv: not in the process list, not in the
  command `:jobs` shows, not in a log. The value is not validated.
- **No rewriting.** A proxy on `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1` is forwarded as
  is. DevDesk does not rewrite it to `host.docker.internal`, does not add
  `--network host` and does not fall back to a direct connection.
- **A `Forward` never prints a value.** `String` and `GoString` show the display
  form (`netproxy.Display`); the values sit behind a function so `fmt` finds
  nothing to print, with any verb.
- **The trust model.** The proxy and its credentials go to every scanner image,
  including one the user set through `tool.Image` (see `scanning.md`).
- **Stderr is redacted.** `cliRunner.Run` redacts each stderr line before it goes
  to `progressFn`, and `waitErr` redacts the diagnostic kept in the `exitError`,
  with `Forward.Redactor` / `Forward.Redact`. A raw proxy value that carries
  credentials becomes its display form (or `[redacted]` when it cannot be parsed),
  and the userinfo and the password disappear, as written, as Go escapes them and
  decoded. A value with no credentials is left alone. The limits are in
  `scanning.md`.

  loopback (`Forward.Loopback`, first the HTTPS pair; `localhost` exactly and
  loopback IPs, not `*.localhost`) and a containerised tool is about to run,

  scanner containers cannot reach it` (`scan.ContainerProxyWarning`; the variable
  is named as read, the value in display form). The router posts it when a scan

    `containers.conf` with `netns = "host"`), the proxy is reachable and the
    warning is wrong. DevDesk does not read the engine configuration.
  - Over-reporting: a scan (`KindScan`) takes every tool the enabled categories

    container that the run will not use.

  verified. Documentation says `-e NAME` without a value reads the client's
  environment, which is what the design relies on; it has not been checked by hand
  here.

forward. Like the HTTP guard it parses the production sources of the module

| Rule | Reported |
|---|---|
| C1 | a `[]string` literal whose first element is the literal `"run"` |
| C2 | a call with the literal `"run"` as argument 0 or 1 and at least one argument after it |

The one allowed site is `containerRun.cmd` in `internal/scan/container_run.go`,
hard-coded in the test. Everything else needs an entry in `containerExceptions`,
matched by file, function and rule, and named in this section
(`TestNetworkDocListsEveryContainerException`);
`TestContainerGuardEveryExceptionStillMatches` fails on a stale one.

| File | Func | Rule | Reason | Until |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `internal/docker/launch.go` | `buildLaunchArgs` | C1 | the user's own container, configured in the launch form: not a scanner | permanent |
| `internal/docker/launch.go` | `VerifyEntrypoint` | C2 | runs only `command -v`, nothing to forward | permanent |

What the guard does not see:

- a `"run"` that is not a literal: built at run time, or a named constant;
- `append(args, "run")` (the literal is neither a first element nor a call
  argument followed by another);
- the `container run` spelling, `"container", "run"` (C2 only looks at
  arguments 0 and 1 for `"run"`, so `"run"` at index 1 is seen only when the first
  one is a different literal, and a longer prefix is not);
- a `"run"` at argument index 2 or later;
- C1 looks at the first element only: `[]string{"--rm", "run"}` is not reported;
- a launch that is not a `run` (`docker create`, `exec`), and clients built in
  third-party code.
'''

open(p,'w').write(s)

p='docs/architecture/network.md'
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index("### Go behaviors to keep in mind"):]
new='''### Go behaviors to keep in mind

Which variables are read, and how:

- `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`, each in two casings. The upper
  case name wins over the lower case one, and an empty value counts as not
  defined (`firstNonEmpty`, like Go's `getEnvAny`).
- `ALL_PROXY` and `FTP_PROXY` are not read, by Go or by DevDesk.
- The environment is read once per process (`http.ProxyFromEnvironment` caches
  it; `ContainerForward` does the same with `sync.OnceValue`). A context switch
  reads nothing again: the user restarts DevDesk after changing a variable. So
  `t.Setenv` has no effect after the first call. A test that needs a given
  environment runs the code in a subprocess, or injects a `Selector` (or, for the
  containers, swaps the `proxyForward` seam of `internal/scan`).
- `NO_PROXY` takes a host name (it also covers its subdomains), `.suffix`
  (subdomains only), an IP address, a CIDR, `host:port`, and `*` (everything).
- `localhost` (exactly) and loopback addresses are never proxied by
  `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`, whatever the variables say; `*.localhost` names
  are proxied.
- CGI: when `REQUEST_METHOD` is set Go refuses `HTTP_PROXY` (see the Proxy row
  above). The container forward does not look at it: a value is forwarded as is.
- socks5 proxies: the HTTPS monitor accepts them (`net/http` does), the SSL
  check refuses them with `StepScheme` and no new dependency. The gap is
  deliberate and known.

Who follows these variables after DEVDESK-581 and DEVDESK-582:

- The HTTP/HTTPS monitor, the SSL monitor and the certificate viewer: the entry
  point above (DEVDESK-581).
- The Diagnostics: direct on purpose (decision Q1). The Proxy row says which
  proxy would apply; no check is sent to a proxy (DEVDESK-582).
- The scanner containers: see the next section (DEVDESK-583).
- Image pulls done by the engine: the Docker or Podman daemon pulls, with its own
  proxy configuration (the service environment, Docker Desktop settings, the
  Podman machine). DevDesk does not configure it and does not pass its variables
  to it. DevDesk's own registry calls (`internal/oci`) go through the entry point.
- `git` (clone, sync) is a child process: it inherits the environment and reads
  it with libcurl's rules, not Go's. libcurl ignores an upper case `HTTP_PROXY`
  for `http://` URLs (only `http_proxy` counts), reads `all_proxy`, and its
  support for CIDR in `NO_PROXY` depends on the curl version. `http.proxy` in the
  git configuration wins. DevDesk does nothing to reconcile the two.

## Container scanners and the proxy (DEVDESK-583)

A scanner that runs from an image (trivy, gitleaks, cosign, plumber,
kubeconform with helm and kustomize, and the version probe of a tool image) has
its own network stack and does not see this process's environment. DevDesk
forwards the proxy itself.

- **One constructor.** `scan.containerRun` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`) is
  the only place that builds `<engine> run --rm`. Its `cmd()` writes
  `run --rm <Flags> -e NAME ... <Image> <Argv>`. Every launcher (`trivy_args.go`,
  `gitleaks.go`, `cosign.go`, `plumber.go`, `kubeconform.go`,
  `kubeconform_render.go`, `tool_source.go`) goes through it.
- **Names in argv, values in the environment.** `netproxy.ContainerForward()`
  returns a `Forward`, a snapshot of `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`
  taken once. For each of the three, the first non-empty value of the upper then
  lower case name is given to both casings. `cmd()` adds `-e NAME` (no value) for
  each name, in the order of `ForwardedVariables`, and sets the values on the
  child process through `Forward.Environ(os.Environ())` (the six names are
  removed from the base first). The engine copies the client's value, so a
  credential in a proxy URL is in no argv: not in the process list, not in the
  command `:jobs` shows, not in a log. The value is not validated.
- **No rewriting.** A proxy on `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1` is forwarded as
  is. DevDesk does not rewrite it to `host.docker.internal`, does not add
  `--network host` and does not fall back to a direct connection.
- **A `Forward` never prints a value.** `String` and `GoString` show the display
  form (`netproxy.Display`); the values sit behind a function so `fmt` finds
  nothing to print, with any verb.
- **The trust model.** The proxy and its credentials go to every scanner image,
  including one the user set through `tool.Image` (see `scanning.md`).
- **Stderr is redacted.** `cliRunner.Run` redacts each stderr line before it goes
  to `progressFn`, and `waitErr` redacts the diagnostic kept in the `exitError`,
  with `Forward.Redactor` / `Forward.Redact`. A raw proxy value that carries
  credentials becomes its display form (or `[redacted]` when it cannot be parsed),
  and the userinfo and the password disappear, as written, as Go escapes them and
  decoded. A value with no credentials is left alone. The limits are in
  `scanning.md`.
- **The loopback warning.** When the HTTPS or HTTP value names this machine's
  loopback (`Forward.Loopback`, first the HTTPS pair; `localhost` exactly and
  loopback IPs, not `*.localhost`) and a containerised tool is about to run,
  the footer says `<VARIABLE> is <scheme://host:port>, on this machine's loopback:
  scanner containers cannot reach it` (`scan.ContainerProxyWarning`; the variable
  is named as read, the value in display form). The router posts it when a scan
  or a verified pull starts, and the Remediation tab when it scans candidates
  (see `app-shell.md`). It is a warning: the scan still starts.
  - False positive: if the engine's default network is `host` (Podman
    `containers.conf` with `netns = "host"`), the proxy is reachable and the
    warning is wrong. DevDesk does not read the engine configuration.
  - Over-reporting: a scan (`KindScan`) takes every tool the enabled categories
    require, while a scan of images runs only trivy. The warning can name a
    container that the run will not use.
- **Podman on a remote machine** (a Podman machine on macOS or Windows): to be
  verified. Documentation says `-e NAME` without a value reads the client's
  environment, which is what the design relies on; it has not been checked by hand
  here.

### The container guard

`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go` keeps a launch from skipping the
forward. Like the HTTP guard it parses the production sources of the module
(go/ast, no types; test files, `.worktrees`, `.git`, `vendor`, `testdata`,
`docs-site` and `node_modules` skipped, `internal/netproxy` read) and reports:

| Rule | Reported |
|---|---|
| C1 | a `[]string` literal whose first element is the literal `"run"` |
| C2 | a call with the literal `"run"` as argument 0 or 1 and at least one argument after it |

The one allowed site is `containerRun.cmd` in `internal/scan/container_run.go`,
hard-coded in the test. Everything else needs an entry in `containerExceptions`,
matched by file, function and rule, and named in this section
(`TestNetworkDocListsEveryContainerException`);
`TestContainerGuardEveryExceptionStillMatches` fails on a stale one.

| File | Func | Rule | Reason | Until |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `internal/docker/launch.go` | `buildLaunchArgs` | C1 | the user's own container, configured in the launch form: not a scanner | permanent |
| `internal/docker/launch.go` | `VerifyEntrypoint` | C2 | runs only `command -v`, nothing to forward | permanent |

What the guard does not see:

- a `"run"` that is not a literal: built at run time, or a named constant;
- `append(args, "run")` (the literal is neither a first element nor a call
  argument followed by another);
- the `container run` spelling, `"container", "run"` (C2 only looks at
  arguments 0 and 1 for `"run"`, so `"run"` at index 1 is seen only when the first
  one is a different literal, and a longer prefix is not);
- a `"run"` at argument index 2 or later;
- C1 looks at the first element only: `[]string{"--rm", "run"}` is not reported;
- a launch that is not a `run` (`docker create`, `exec`), and clients built in
  third-party code.
'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

cat > docs-site/docs/how-to/work-behind-a-proxy.md <<'EOF'
# Work behind a proxy

DevDesk follows the standard proxy variables of your shell. This guide says which
ones, what each part of DevDesk does with them, and what to do when a scanner
container cannot reach your proxy. For the design, see
[Network](../explanation/network.md#the-proxy-variables) and
[Security Scanning](../explanation/scanning.md#behind-a-proxy).

## Set the variables

Export them before you start DevDesk:

```bash
export HTTPS_PROXY=REDACTED
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.example:3128
export NO_PROXY=localhost,.corp.example,10.0.0.0/8
dk
```

What DevDesk reads:

| Variable | Notes |
|---|---|
| `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy` | the proxy for `https://` targets |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `http_proxy` | the proxy for `http://` targets |
| `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy` | what goes direct |

- The upper case name wins over the lower case one. An empty value counts as not
  set.
- `ALL_PROXY` is not read.
- DevDesk reads the variables **once, when it starts**. A context switch does not
  read them again. After you change a variable, restart DevDesk.
- `NO_PROXY` takes a host name (it covers its subdomains), `.suffix` (subdomains
  only), an IP address, a CIDR, `host:port`, and `*`.
- `localhost` and loopback addresses always go direct. `*.localhost` names do not:
  they go through the proxy.

## Monitors

The HTTP and HTTPS monitors and the SSL monitor take the same path, so a host is
no longer green on HTTP and red on SSL behind a proxy. A `socks5` proxy works for
the HTTPS monitor, and the SSL check refuses it. When the proxy refuses the
`CONNECT`, select the DOWN row on the Certificates tab: the footer says which step
failed.

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics measure the **direct** path from this machine, on purpose. They
never send a check to a proxy. The **Proxy** row tells you whether a proxy
variable applies to the target: configured (with its address, without any
credential), excluded by `NO_PROXY`, not used for a loopback target, invalid, or
none. When the direct connection fails and a proxy applies, the TCP row says so:
a closed direct path is expected behind a mandatory proxy.

## Scanner containers

When a scanner runs from an image (Docker or Podman), DevDesk passes `HTTP_PROXY`,
`HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` to the container, in both casings. The values travel
in the environment of the engine command. They never appear in the command line,
in `:jobs` or in a log, and DevDesk removes proxy credentials from the tool's error
output.

Two things to know:

- The proxy and its credentials go to every scanner image, including an image you
  set with `tool.Image`. Use only images you trust.
- DevDesk does not validate the values and does not rewrite them.

### The loopback warning

A container has its own loopback. If a variable names `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or
`::1`, the container cannot reach it, and a scan that starts shows this warning in
the footer:

```text
HTTPS_PROXY is http://127.0.0.1:3128, on this machine's loopback: scanner containers cannot reach it
```

The scan still starts and will probably fail to connect. Choose one:

1. Make the proxy reachable from the container: listen on an address the
   container can route to (not only `127.0.0.1`), and set the variable to that
   address.
2. Run the tools as local binaries: set `scan.tools.<tool>.source: binary` (see
   [Locating the tools](../explanation/scanning.md#locating-the-tools)). A binary
   runs on this machine and reaches the local proxy.

The warning can be wrong. If your engine runs containers on the host network
(for example Podman with `netns = "host"` in `containers.conf`), the proxy is
reachable and you can ignore it. It can also name a container the run does not
use: a scan of an image runs only Trivy.

## Image pulls and the engine

The Docker or Podman daemon pulls images, with **its own** proxy configuration:
the service environment on Linux, the Proxies settings of Docker Desktop, the
configuration of the Podman machine. DevDesk does not set it. If a pull fails
behind a proxy, fix the engine's configuration. DevDesk's own registry calls
follow the variables above.

## git

Cloning and syncing run `git`, which reads the variables with libcurl's rules, not
DevDesk's:

- an upper case `HTTP_PROXY` is ignored for `http://` URLs (use `http_proxy`);
- `all_proxy` and `ALL_PROXY` are read;
- CIDR ranges in `NO_PROXY` depend on your curl version;
- `http.proxy` in your git configuration wins over the variables.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| A variable you changed has no effect | DevDesk reads them once | Restart DevDesk |
| The Proxy row says `Invalid HTTPS_PROXY value` | The value is not a usable proxy URL | Write it as `http://host:port` |
| Footer warning about a loopback proxy | The container cannot reach this machine's loopback | See [the loopback warning](#the-loopback-warning) |
| Hosts in `NO_PROXY` still go through the proxy | `*.localhost`, or a form the matcher does not know | Check the form against the list above |
EOF

# Work behind a proxy

DevDesk follows the standard proxy variables of your shell. This guide says which
ones, what each part of DevDesk does with them, and what to do when a scanner
container cannot reach your proxy. For the design, see
[Network](../explanation/network.md#the-proxy-variables) and
[Security Scanning](../explanation/scanning.md#behind-a-proxy).

## Set the variables

Export them before you start DevDesk:

```bash
export HTTPS_PROXY=REDACTED
export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.example:3128
export NO_PROXY=localhost,.corp.example,10.0.0.0/8
dk
```

What DevDesk reads:

| Variable | Notes |
|---|---|
| `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy` | the proxy for `https://` targets |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `http_proxy` | the proxy for `http://` targets |
| `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy` | what goes direct |

- The upper case name wins over the lower case one. An empty value counts as not
  set.
- `ALL_PROXY` is not read.
- DevDesk reads the variables **once, when it starts**. A context switch does not
  read them again. After you change a variable, restart DevDesk.
- `NO_PROXY` takes a host name (it covers its subdomains), `.suffix` (subdomains
  only), an IP address, a CIDR, `host:port`, and `*`.
- `localhost` and loopback addresses always go direct. `*.localhost` names do not:
  they go through the proxy.

## Monitors

The HTTP and HTTPS monitors and the SSL monitor take the same path, so a host is
no longer green on HTTP and red on SSL behind a proxy. A `socks5` proxy works for
the HTTPS monitor, and the SSL check refuses it. When the proxy refuses the
`CONNECT`, select the DOWN row on the Certificates tab: the footer says which step
failed.

## Diagnostics

The Diagnostics measure the **direct** path from this machine, on purpose. They
never send a check to a proxy. The **Proxy** row tells you whether a proxy
variable applies to the target: configured (with its address, without any
credential), excluded by `NO_PROXY`, not used for a loopback target, invalid, or
none. When the direct connection fails and a proxy applies, the TCP row says so:
a closed direct path is expected behind a mandatory proxy.

## Scanner containers

When a scanner runs from an image (Docker or Podman), DevDesk passes `HTTP_PROXY`,
`HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` to the container, in both casings. The values travel
in the environment of the engine command. They never appear in the command line,
in `:jobs` or in a log, and DevDesk removes proxy credentials from the tool's error
output.

Two things to know:

- The proxy and its credentials go to every scanner image, including an image you
  set with `tool.Image`. Use only images you trust.
- DevDesk does not validate the values and does not rewrite them.

### The loopback warning

A container has its own loopback. If a variable names `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or
`::1`, the container cannot reach it, and a scan that starts shows this warning in
the footer:

```text
HTTPS_PROXY is http://127.0.0.1:3128, on this machine's loopback: scanner containers cannot reach it
```

The scan still starts and will probably fail to connect. Choose one:

1. Make the proxy reachable from the container: listen on an address the
   container can route to (not only `127.0.0.1`), and set the variable to that
   address.
2. Run the tools as local binaries: set `scan.tools.<tool>.source: binary` (see
   [Locating the tools](../explanation/scanning.md#locating-the-tools)). A binary
   runs on this machine and reaches the local proxy.

The warning can be wrong. If your engine runs containers on the host network
(for example Podman with `netns = "host"` in `containers.conf`), the proxy is
reachable and you can ignore it. It can also name a container the run does not
use: a scan of an image runs only Trivy.

## Image pulls and the engine

The Docker or Podman daemon pulls images, with **its own** proxy configuration:
the service environment on Linux, the Proxies settings of Docker Desktop, the
configuration of the Podman machine. DevDesk does not set it. If a pull fails
behind a proxy, fix the engine's configuration. DevDesk's own registry calls
follow the variables above.

## git

Cloning and syncing run `git`, which reads the variables with libcurl's rules, not
DevDesk's:

- an upper case `HTTP_PROXY` is ignored for `http://` URLs (use `http_proxy`);
- `all_proxy` and `ALL_PROXY` are read;
- CIDR ranges in `NO_PROXY` depend on your curl version;
- `http.proxy` in your git configuration wins over the variables.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| A variable you changed has no effect | DevDesk reads them once | Restart DevDesk |
| The Proxy row says `Invalid HTTPS_PROXY value` | The value is not a usable proxy URL | Write it as `http://host:port` |
| Footer warning about a loopback proxy | The container cannot reach this machine's loopback | See [the loopback warning](#the-loopback-warning) |
| Hosts in `NO_PROXY` still go through the proxy | `*.localhost`, or a form the matcher does not know | Check the form against the list above |
EOF
